title: Default run stays review-only; the medium+fix:true path finally ran 2026-06-20T04:11 and applied 2 fixes
detail: Most orchestrator runs stay review-only (review.fix.mode='review-only'). EXCEPTION 2026-06-20T04:11: a lanes:[review] run with effort:medium+fix:true ran the review-optimize fix path, applied 2 fixes (code-knowledge.ts + knowledge-db.ts hardcoded absolute user path -> REPO_DIR-derived), 0 regressions, tests 546->546 pass. This is the FIRST non-zero-fix run in this history (all prior runs were review-only or applied 0). The ux lane auto-applies its own 3 fixes via its own dryRun:false path, independent of review fix.mode. The medium-effort review fix path is now VERIFIED WORKING (was previously 'unverified' in this history).

title: openIssues trend is wildly non-monotone: 11->14->12->1->0->21->172->174->22->19->10->1->26->0 across runs; code churn refills the queue
detail: openIssues went 11,14,12,1,0,21,172,174,22,19,10,1,26,0. The 0->21->172->174 escalation after the 06-16 clean run confirmed the baseline was fragile and code churn refills the queue aggressively. The 22->19->10->1 decline on 2026-06-19/2026-06-20T03:22 reflected shrinking changed-file surface PLUS post-W4 verify filtering. 2026-06-20T04:11 JUMPED back to 26 (verified=26, adversarial 2/2 upheld) — BUT this was an effort:medium FULL-scope scan (191 files, targetScope:'full'), not an incremental one. So the 26 is a full-surface count, NOT a regression of the incremental trend. 2026-06-20T06:07 returned to openIssues=0 on a 2-file incremental scope (verified=0, adversarial rejected the sole finding). Treat a 0 as 'queue drained', never 'nothing to find'. NOTE: post-W4 the openIssues count reflects verified (post-filter), so it can be lower than raw newFindings. IMPORTANT: openIssues magnitude is only comparable across runs at the SAME scan scope (incremental vs full).

title: schema runtime lane reports ~5 findings on dirty runs, null once, FOUR consecutive fully-clean 0s
detail: Runtime lane reported ~5 findings on non-clean runs (first run had 8 + 2 errors). On 2026-06-18T13:32 it returned null; on 2026-06-18T15:22, 2026-06-19T18:35, 2026-06-19T21:01, AND 2026-06-19T21:56 it returned runtimeFindings=0, runtimeErrors=0, driftRemaining=0 — FOUR consecutive fully-clean schema lane results. The runtime lane (buildCliArgs->run.py boundary) is productive on churn but goes quiet when the tree is clean; a 0 is now firmly interpretable as clean (distinct from the null failure mode). Check schemaHistory path when schema=null.

title: runtimeErrors only appeared in the first run (2); zero across all 10 runs since
detail: First run had 2 runtimeErrors + 8 runtimeFindings; all subsequent runs (now 10 total) have 0 errors, including the latest fully-clean 0-finding run. Either the boundary stabilized or earlier runs' findings were resolved out-of-band. Don't assume errors are gone — re-run objective:runtime after any CLI change.

title: coverageDelta is NaN on every run — coverage lane never runs under objective:runtime
detail: All runs set objective:runtime (default), so coverageDelta reports 'NaN' every time (now 9 runs confirmed). To get a real coverage trend you must pass objective:coverage|both|all; the default lane produces no coverage signal.

title: driftRemaining is 0 on all runs — GUI<->run.py flags stay aligned
detail: driftRemaining=0 across all runs (now 9 with signal). Either drift is genuinely clean or check:schema was already applied earlier. Drift lane is currently a low-value no-op; budget agent time on the runtime lane instead.

title: Verified review findings severity is run-dependent; medium dominates incremental high-volume runs, low dominates full-scope scans, critical is volume-orthogonal
detail: Severity distribution varies per run. 2026-06-18T13:32: high=5, medium=12, low=4. 2026-06-18T15:22: high=6, medium=13, low=2. 2026-06-19T18:35: high=2, medium=3, low=4 (lowest total=9, low-dominant). 2026-06-19T21:01: high=3, medium=15, low=4 (total=22, MEDIUM-dominant). 2026-06-19T21:56: critical=1, high=4, medium=8, low=6 (total=19). 2026-06-19T22:46: critical=1, high=1, medium=4, low=4 (total=10, low TIES medium). 2026-06-20T03:22: medium=1 (total VERIFIED=1). 2026-06-20T04:11 (effort:medium FULL scope): high=2, medium=6, low=16, info=2 (total VERIFIED=26) — the first run with an `info` bucket, and LOW dominates because a full-scope scan surfaces many low-severity style/quality nits the incremental scans skip. 2026-06-20T06:07: VERIFIED=0 (1 finding rejected by adversarial; no bySeverity buckets populated). Pattern sharpens: medium is the modal bucket on incremental high-volume runs (>=12); on a FULL-scope run LOW dominates (style nits); high stays in a narrow 1-6 band; critical is rare (2 in 14 runs) but when it appears it is the highest-priority fix target regardless of total volume.

title: review-only runs report findings but don't fix them; openIssues only drops via fix:true, external action, OR verify-gate filtering
detail: Most runs have review.fix.mode='review-only' (fix:false). The 11->1->0 openIssues drop between 06-15 and 06-16 happened WITHOUT any review fix:true run — the backlog was cleared outside the orchestrator. The 0->21->172->174 escalation confirmed the queue refills as code changes. EXCEPTION 2026-06-20T04:11: an effort:medium+fix:true run applied 2 fixes (0 regressions), proving the fix path DOES clear high-severity findings when invoked. Each review-only run is a fresh newFindings snapshot, not a persistent tracker. NOTE: the 22->19->10->1->0 decline on 06-19/06-20T03:22/06-20T06:07 reflected shrinking changed-file surface AND post-W4 verify-gate filtering. A clean review-only run is not evidence the code is clean, only that nothing new was flagged.

title: delta_from_last is null on every run — inter-run delta tracking is not wired
detail: signals.delta_from_last is null in all runs (2026-06-20T06:07 confirms again), so you cannot read 'better/worse than last run' from the envelope. Compute deltas yourself from openIssues/verified/runtimeFindings across history files — but only compare runs at the SAME scan scope (incremental vs full).

title: Orchestrator completes with empty phases_failed on every run
detail: status='complete' and phases_failed=[] on all runs, even ones that surfaced runtimeErrors, 174 openIssues, or a null schema lane. Don't treat 'complete' as 'no problems' — phase success only means the lane ran, not that the code is healthy. Read result.review/schema/ux for actual signal.

title: dirtyTree was false on all runs INCLUDING the first fix:true run — the dirty-tree downgrade never fired (every fix:true opportunity landed on a clean tree)
detail: dirtyTree was false in all runs. 2026-06-20T04:11 was the FIRST fix:true run (effort:medium): treeDirty=false, dirtyFilesBefore=[], so the fix path proceeded and applied 2 fixes. This means the 'fix:true gets downgraded to review-only on a dirty git tree' guard still has NOT actually fired here (every fix:true opportunity landed on a clean tree). The guard's downgrade behavior remains unverified — test it deliberately (stage uncommitted WIP, then invoke fix:true) before trusting it rejects the fix.

title: SUPERSEDED: verified != newFindings once the W4 consolidated verify gate runs — see gotcha-verified-neq-newfindings
detail: Originally recorded (2026-06-14..2026-06-19) that result.review.verified always equals result.review.newFindings (no verify filtering). SUPERSEDED by 2026-06-20T03:22: that run had newFindings=4 but verified=1 — the W4 consolidated adversarial-verify gate (EFFORT_CONFIG.low.adversarial changed from 'skip' to fail-open-filter) now rejects findings, so verified can be strictly LESS than newFindings. The equality held only because the pre-W4 gate was skipped. This record is kept for trend continuity; read gotcha-verified-neq-newfindings for current behavior.

title: schema lane can silently return null — but also returns full data when healthy (intermittent)
detail: On 2026-06-18T13:32 the schema result field was null despite schema being in lanes. The 2026-06-18T15:22, 2026-06-19T18:35, 2026-06-19T21:01, and 2026-06-19T21:56 runs show the lane CAN return full data (runtimeFindings=0, driftRemaining=0) — so null is a genuine intermittent failure mode, not a constant. The schemaHistory path (gui-movie-director-schema-self-improve/iterations.jsonl) is the authoritative log; null result may mean internal error. Always check schemaHistory when schema=null. NOTE: on 2026-06-19T22:46, 2026-06-20T03:22, 2026-06-20T04:11, AND 2026-06-20T06:07 the runs used lanes:['review'] ONLY (no schema lane requested), so schema=null is EXPECTED and NOT a failure — distinguish 'schema not requested' (lanes omits 'schema'/'all') from 'schema requested but returned null' before diagnosing an intermittent failure.

title: No stable baseline: clean runs are immediately re-broken by code churn; full-scope scans reset the count
detail: The 2026-06-16 clean run (openIssues=0) was broken within hours — 21, 172, 174, then 22, 19, 10, 1 (incremental, post-W4). 2026-06-20T04:11 was effort:medium FULL-scope (191 files) and reported openIssues=26 — a different MAGNITUDE because it is a full-surface count, not incremental. No clean baseline has survived to the next run. Re-establishing a baseline requires a fix:true run to clear the queue AND a code-churn freeze; review-only runs cannot produce a durable baseline. Compare only runs at the SAME scan scope when trending.

title: SUPERSEDED: the 21-finding spike was dwarfed by a 172-finding run hours later
detail: Recorded the 2026-06-18T13:32 21-finding spike as the largest single-run count. SUPERSEDED by openissues-172-spike-three-lane which shows the same code-churn driver producing 172 findings (8x larger) just hours later, and the non-monotone pattern (openissues-converges-to-zero) is the durable insight. This specific spike magnitude is no longer the high-water mark.

title: 174 openIssues high-water mark was a 3-lane ux-contaminated run; post-uxAuto-fix pure-code runs sit ~1-26 (scope-dependent)
detail: The 2026-06-19T18:35 run produced 174 openIssues = review.newFindings(9) + ux.totalIssues(165), ~95% ux-sourced. That was the high-water mark UNDER the old openIssues formula (review+schema+drift+ux). After the uxAuto gate fix (2026-06-19T18:51), the pure review-only/review+schema runs produced openIssues=22, 19, 10, 1 (incremental) — and 2026-06-20T04:11 (effort:medium FULL-scope) produced 26 (verified=26, adversarial 2/2 upheld). The 26 is a full-surface count, NOT comparable to the incremental 1/10/19/22 figures. When ux lane is enabled, openIssues is NOT comparable to review-only figures — always split result.ux.totalIssues from result.review.newFindings before trending. Also: never trend a full-scope count against an incremental count.

title: ux totalIssues (165) dwarfs review newFindings (9) — openIssues stops being a review-only metric
detail: Second ux-lane run: ux.totalIssues=165 vs review.newFindings=9; merged openIssues=174 was ~95% ux-sourced (up from 88% on the first ux run, because review findings shrank 21->9 while ux held ~150-165). Treating openIssues as a code-review regression signal is invalid once ux lane is enabled — ux surveys every view's UX issues (field clarity, loading states, empty states), a different and much larger population than code bugs. Always read result.ux.totalIssues separately from result.review.newFindings; never trend them together as one number.

title: ux auto-fix lifts avg score ~0.5 points per run fixing only 3 of ~150 issues
detail: The 2026-06-18T15:22 ux lane surveyed 23 views (avg 4.82/10) and auto-fixed 3 issues, raising the average to 5.36/10 (+0.54). The 2026-06-19T18:35 run surveyed 23 views (avg 3.91/10) and auto-fixed 3 issues, raising to 4.43/10 (+0.52). The ux fix path is functional and applies fixes via its own dryRun:false control — independent of review.fix.mode (which stayed review-only). The +0.5/3-fix lever ratio is consistent across two runs. Note: avg DROPPED 5.36->3.91 between runs (different view mix / churn re-introduced regressions), so absolute score is not yet monotone — but the per-run fix delta is stable. (The review lane's fix path is ALSO now verified working as of 2026-06-20T04:11 — see lever-medium-fix-applies-real-fixes.)

title: UX avg score baseline hovers ~4-5/10 across 23 views; absolute score is non-monotone run-to-run
detail: Two ux-lane baselines now: 2026-06-18T15:22 avgScoreBefore=4.82, 2026-06-19T18:35 avgScoreBefore=3.91 (DOWN 0.91 despite a +0.52 fix delta the prior run). The before-score dropped because code churn re-introduced UX regressions between runs. Even after fixing 3 each time, avg only reaches ~4.4-5.4/10. The UX surface has significant debt (field clarity, loading states, empty states) that the review/schema lanes cannot surface, AND fixes do not durably stick — the same views re-regress. The ux lane is the only lane that sees this surface; it is additive signal, but a single fix run is not durable without a code-churn freeze.

title: schema lane returned a fully-clean result (0 findings, 0 errors, 0 drift) — now FOUR consecutive clean runs
detail: 2026-06-18T15:22 was the first schema lane result with runtimeFindings=0, runtimeErrors=0, AND driftRemaining=0 simultaneously; 2026-06-19T18:35, 2026-06-19T21:01, and 2026-06-19T21:56 repeat it. Prior clean-ish runs still had a few runtime findings or a null result. Four consecutive clean runs suggest the schema->CLI boundary (buildCliArgs->run.py) is currently healthy — the GUI schemas and run.py flags are aligned. Re-confirm after any CLI/schema edit; a 0 is now interpretable as genuinely clean (distinct from the null failure mode).

title: Command views render a blank/black main panel with no form on first navigation
detail: The dominant UX defect class: several views (t2i, video-quality, video-generate, faceswap, model-check, jobs) render an empty black void on first load because CommandForm only mounts AFTER useDefaultState resolves server defaults, and the canvas is bare in the meantime. There is no header, breadcrumb, empty-state, or loading skeleton — the user cannot tell a loading failure from an empty state from a broken render. Affects every createCommandView() view until guarded. The VLM caption reads these as 'a large, empty black panel' / 'no primary action button visible'.

title: Guard CommandViewShell with an actionable empty-state instead of a dead black panel
detail: Adopted fix for blank-panel views: when a view yields no form children (silent render failure), CommandViewShell now renders an actionable 'This view has nothing to show' message plus a .empty-view-state CSS class, so the canvas is never a bare void. Applied to video-quality-01 (score held 2->2 but the panel is no longer dead). Generalizes to every createCommandView view — always provide a non-blocking empty/loading placeholder while useDefaultState resolves or when children fail to mount.

title: Wrap command views in a persistent title header (reuse ModelCheckView inline-style convention)
detail: Adopted fix for blank/unlabeled panels: wrap the generated view (e.g. T2lView) in a container that renders a persistent h2 title plus a dim description line, matching the existing ModelCheckView inline-style convention and reusing --text-bright/--text-dim CSS variables. Result: the main panel is never blank/unlabeled and the user can always tell which view is active. Applied to t2i-01 (score 3->9). This is the higher-impact sibling of the empty-state guard — it also labels healthy renders.

title: Sidebar active-state logic is correct; the CSS is too faint for the VLM (and users) to read as selected
detail: Layout.tsx already computes an `active` class on the sidebar item when currentView.action===cmd.id, so the routing logic is NOT the bug. The defect is that .sidebar-item.active (global.css:91) uses only a faint background + accent left border + accent text that reads as indistinguishable from inactive. Strengthen with an --accent color-mix tinted background + font-weight 600 (adopted in video-quality-02, score 2->8) so the selected item is unmistakable. Do NOT re-investigate the Layout logic when the active cue looks missing.

title: toSections silently discards any schema field without a `section` property
detail: Latent trap: schemas/toForm.ts toSections does `if (!f.section) continue;`, so any field lacking a `section` is silently dropped from the rendered form with NO error. Confirmed instance: faceswap schema's 'LoRA Path' field {key:'lora'} has no section, so the documented LoRA control never appears in the UI and users cannot set a custom face-swap LoRA despite the schema declaring it. Either assign every schema field a section, or make toSections fall back to a default 'Advanced' section instead of dropping sectionless fields.

title: ViewDescriptor id MUST equal the useCommandJob/SCHEMA_MAP action key
detail: Latent routing/state bug: VideoGenerateView registers with descriptor id 'vid-generate', but every other reference uses 'video-generate' (useCommandJob('video-generate'), action='video-generate', SCHEMA_MAP['video-generate']). If routing or useDefaultState keys off the descriptor id, the schema-defaults fetch and action routing resolve against different keys — contributing to blank render and breaking per-view state persistence. Convention: keep the descriptor id identical to the schema action key AND the CLI action, as the sibling video views (VideoRelay etc.) already do.

title: Disabled submit buttons give no reason — no inline hint listing missing required inputs
detail: Recurring UX gap: schema.isDisabled(state) returns true when required inputs are unset (e.g. faceswap input_image/face), greying out the primary action, but nothing in the UI explains WHY or what the user must do. No required-field callout, no helper text, no 'Upload X and Y to enable Z'. A first-time user staring at a disabled button has no path forward. When schema.isDisabled(state) is true, render an InlineError or small hint near the btn-row listing the missing required inputs.

title: Sidebar nav items are non-semantic divs — not keyboard-focusable, no aria-current
detail: Accessibility defect: all navigation entries (Gallery, Config, Jobs, every command) are plain <div> elements with onClick handlers (Layout.tsx). No role='button', no tabIndex, no aria-current — invisible to Tab-key navigation and screen readers cannot announce them. The sidebar <aside> is also not a <nav aria-label>. Fix: render nav items as <button> (or role='button' tabIndex={0} + onKeyDown Enter/Space), wrap in <nav aria-label='Views'>, set aria-current='page' on the active item. A keyboard-only or assistive-tech user cannot reach any view currently.

title: Avg UX score ~4-5/10; ~3 fixes per run, ~17 high-severity issues remain — needs ~8 iters to reach ~7.0
detail: Measured baseline from the 23-view scan: avg UX score 4.82 (first run) / 3.91 (second run), ~150-165 issues total (~20 high). With maxIters:3 and dryRun:false, only 3 fixes applied per run (score ceiling ~4.4-5.4/10), leaving ~17 high-severity issues unfixed. The blank-panel/active-nav/header fixes each move a single view 3-7 points, so the lever-per-iter ratio is high but the volume of low-scoring views (t2i=3, video-quality=2, video-generate=3, faceswap=3, image-restore=4, model-check=4) exceeds a 3-iter budget. Suggested next run: maxIters:8, dryRun:false -> expect avg ~7.0. image-pipeline scored null/0 issues (healthy / not reached) and can be skipped to save budget.

title: VLM caption can misread a correctly-wired feature as missing when the visual cue is too subtle
detail: Recurring false-positive class: the VLM (and by extension users) reports 'No active/selected highlight' and 'no primary action button visible' even when the underlying TS logic is correct. video-quality-02 and t2i-02 both reported a missing active-nav cue, but Layout.tsx already applies the `active` class — the CSS was just too faint. Treat 'feature is missing' captions as visual-prominence problems first (strengthen the CSS) before investigating the logic. Distinguish 'logic absent' from 'logic present but invisible' by reading the source, not by trusting the caption.

title: Absolute-path-as-info-disclosure is a FALSE POSITIVE when the path is functional identity
detail: Review lane flags api/models.ts handleListLoras/handleListVaes returning absolute filesystem paths to the client as 'info disclosure'. But lora.path is LOAD-BEARING: LoraField.tsx uses it as the <option value>, copy-to-clipboard (for CLI reuse), and the selected value flows to run.py --lora. Stripping to basename BREAKS the selector + copy feature. Verified 2026-06-19: grep frontend shows lora.path used as identity key at LoraField.tsx:165/199/204. Suppress this finding class; the threat model is weak anyway (unauthenticated localhost dev tool).

title: getReader()-throws finding misses the null-stream guard 67 lines above
detail: Review flagged lib/subprocess.ts:210 'getReader() throws outside try/catch, leaves job stuck running'. But a guard at lines 143-152 checks `if (!proc.stdout || !proc.stderr)` and finalizes-as-failed BEFORE the getReader calls are reached. The review lane pattern-matched the call site without scanning upward for an existing guard. Verified 2026-06-19: guard present, finding is dead. Generalizes: review lacks duplicate/guard awareness — always scan surrounding context before applying an error-handling finding.

title: UX auto-detect made the 'cheap routine scan' cost 77 agents/2.6M tok — now gated behind uxAuto:true (gate CONFIRMED working across 7 runs)
detail: A BARE invocation auto-detected the GUI server (Resolve phase) and appended the UX lane, surveying all 23 views. In review-only/dryRun the UX lane fixes 0 issues, so this cost ~50 agents + VLM calls for no actionable output — turning the documented 'cheap review+schema scan' into a 77-agent/2.6M-token/55min run. FIXED 2026-06-19: auto-detect now requires uxAuto:true (default off). Opt in via uxAuto:true or lanes:['ux']/'all'. CONFIRMED across seven runs (2026-06-19T21:01/21:56/22:46, 2026-06-20T03:22, 2026-06-20T04:11, 2026-06-20T06:07): six bare lanes:[review] runs returned ux=null and did NOT spawn the UX lane — the gate holds across consecutive runs, and openIssues returned to pure code-only figures (22, 19, 10, 1, full-scope 26, incremental 0).

title: openIssues now excludes UX noise — code-health debt only (review+schema+drift); CONFIRMED stable across 7 runs (0-26, scope-dependent)
detail: Resolves the openissues-converges-to-zero metric: openIssues was review+schema+drift+ux, so the 174 high-water mark was ~95% unfixed UX (165/174). In review-only the UX lane fixes 0, so the scalar + its run-over-run trend reflected screenshot variance, not code health. FIXED 2026-06-19: openIssues = review verified + schema runtimeErrors + remaining drift. UX tracked separately as uxOpenIssues + avgUxScore. Delta agent recomputes prev from components so the trend stays comparable across the formula change. CONFIRMED across seven runs: 2026-06-19T21:01 openIssues=22, 2026-06-19T21:56=19, 2026-06-19T22:46=10, 2026-06-20T03:22=1 (all incremental, ux excluded), 2026-06-20T04:11=26 (effort:medium FULL-scope, verified=26, adversarial 2/2 upheld) — an order of magnitude below the ux-contaminated 174, a plausible code-health magnitude, and 2026-06-20T06:07=0 (2-file incremental, 1 finding rejected by the gate). NOTE: the 26 is a full-surface count, NOT comparable to the incremental 0/1/10/19/22 trend — only trend runs at the SAME scan scope.

title: Verify a finding's usage + surrounding guards BEFORE applying — effort:low FP rate was ~50% pre-W4; medium+fix:true applied 2 clean fixes 2026-06-20T04:11
detail: On the 2026-06-19 run, 4 of 8 'verified' review findings were false-positive or already-fixed: (1) lora/vae path 'info disclosure' — path is functional identity; (2) subprocess getReader 'throws' — guarded 67 lines above; (3) model-check/config stderr 'leak' — localhost dev tool, forwarding aids debugging. Adversarial verify reported upheld=0 yet 8 stayed 'verified' — it does NOT filter context-free pattern matches. CHECK before applying: grep frontend usage of the flagged symbol AND scan ~70 lines around the site for an existing guard. NOTE: post-W4 (2026-06-20T03:22) the consolidated verify gate now DOES this filtering at verify time (rejected 3/4). UPDATE 2026-06-20T04:11: the effort:medium+fix:true run applied 2 fixes that were REAL bugs (hardcoded absolute user path /Users/huangziyu/... in code-knowledge.ts + knowledge-db.ts -> REPO_DIR-derived portable path, matching sibling lib/paths.ts convention), 0 regressions, tests 546->546 — so the verify+fix path is now producing clean, correct fixes when the findings are genuine.

title: Review finding volume scales with scan scope; effort:medium FULL-scope produced 26 verified (2 high, 6 medium, 16 low, 2 info)
detail: 2026-06-19T21:01 surfaced 22 (verified=22); 2026-06-19T21:56 surfaced 19 (high=4, medium=8, low=6, critical=1). 2026-06-19T22:46 surfaced 10 (high=1, medium=4, low=4, critical=1). 2026-06-20T03:22 surfaced newFindings=4 but verified=1 (W4 gate rejected 3/4, rejection_rate 0.75). 2026-06-20T04:11 (effort:medium FULL-scope, 191 files) surfaced verified=26 (high=2, medium=6, low=16, info=2) with adversarial 2/2 upheld (rejection_rate 0) — the gate RAN (not skipped) but accepted everything, so verified==newFindings==26 this run. 2026-06-20T06:07 (effort:low, 2-file incremental) surfaced newFindings=1, verified=0, adversarial rejected 1/1 (rejection_rate 1.0) — the gate can reject EVERYTHING on a small surface. The full-scope count is much higher than incremental runs because it scans every file (many low-severity style/quality nits the incremental scan skips). Implication for fix-targeting: medium is where actionable (non-FP) debt accumulates on incremental runs; on full-scope LOW dominates (style nits); critical>0 is a fix:true trigger regardless of total. NOTE: W4 gate rejection_rate varies run-to-run (0.75 on 03:22, 0 on 04:11, 1.0 on 06:07) — a 0 rejection_rate means findings were genuinely upheld, NOT that the gate skipped. Pair with lever-w4-consolidated-verify-gate-working.

title: W3 USAGE_AWARE dimension prompts — CONFIRMED working: the chronic localhost-threat FP cluster did NOT recur on incremental OR full-scope scans
detail: Root cause of the ~50% effort:low false-positive rate: the adversarial-verify gate reported upheld=0 yet findings stayed verified (2026-06-19T21:01: 22 verifiedFindings, 0 upheld, 14 in security). Fixed at SOURCE (committed 092e636): in the info-disclosure / error-handling / security dimension prompts of .claude/workflows/gui-movie-director-review-optimize.js, REQUIRE the reviewer to (a) grep call-site usage of the flagged symbol/endpoint and (b) scan ~70 lines around the site plus the auth middleware for an existing guard or benign context BEFORE flagging. CONFIRMED across three scans (2026-06-20T03:22 incremental, 2026-06-20T04:11 FULL-scope 191 files): the chronic FP set (api/models.ts abs-path info-disclosure, api/config.ts verify-python stderr, api/model-check.ts stderr, api/caption.ts validate-path, api/gallery.ts localhost-threat-model) did NOT appear in the findings — W3 prompts suppressed them at flag-time, before any verify gate, even on a full-surface scan. This moves the usage-check from fix-time (pattern-verify-usage-before-applying) to flag-time.

title: Do NOT bulk-apply the effort:low security/info-disclosure cluster via effort:medium+fix:true - adversarial gate was broken (upheld=0); cluster is W3-suppressed
detail: 2026-06-19T21:01 reported 22 verifiedFindings with adversarialUpheld=0 and its nextStep suggested effort:medium+fix:true. Ignore that for the security-dim cluster (api/models.ts listLoras/listVaes abs paths; api/config.ts handleVerifyPython stderr + validatePythonPath substring; api/model-check.ts stderr). review-optimize.knowledge.jsonl already documents several as recurring patterns (verify-python-leaks-stderr, model-check-leaks-stderr, validate-python-path-substring-not-prefix). title: verified can be <, ==, or (historically) != newFindings once the W4 consolidated verify gate runs — read adversarial.totalVerdicts, not the equality
detail: Prior to W4, result.review.verified always equaled result.review.newFindings because the effort:low adversarial gate was SKIPPED (fail-open kept every finding). After W4 (consolidated gate actually filters), verified reflects only the findings that survived adversarial verification. 2026-06-20T03:22: newFindings=4, verified=1 (3 rejected, rejection_rate 0.75). 2026-06-20T04:11: newFindings=26, verified=26 (0 rejected, rejection_rate 0.0, 2/2 upheld) — the gate RAN but accepted everything. 2026-06-20T06:07: newFindings=1, verified=0 (1 rejected, rejection_rate 1.0) — the gate rejected the SOLE finding, dropping verified to 0 and openIssues to 0. Practical implications: (1) openIssues uses the verified count, so it undercounts raw findings when the gate rejects; check result.findings.total vs verified. (2) bySeverity counts VERIFIED findings only (so a rejection_rate=1.0 run has an EMPTY bySeverity map, as seen 2026-06-20T06:07). (3) When comparing to pre-W4 history, note the semantics change. (4) CRITICAL: verified==newFindings is NOT proof the gate skipped post-W4 — a full-scope scan with genuine findings can have 0 rejections. Read result.adversarial.totalVerdicts: 0 = gate did not run on any finding; >0 = gate ran. Supersedes review-verified-equals-newfindings.

title: useJobs listens for a 'job_start' WS message type the server NEVER broadcasts — stale jobs list for up to 5s after spawn
detail: The single verified finding from 2026-06-20T03:22 (correctness, medium, confidence 92): frontend/hooks/queries/useJobs.ts:16 registers a useWebSocketEvents callback that revalidates (mutate()) on msg.type==='job_complete'||'job_failed'||'job_start', but a grep of EVERY broadcast site (api/ws.ts:108 emits only job_complete/job_failed/log; server.ts:92/114 and api/bundle.ts:58 emit only hmr-reload/gallery-updated/hmr-error; ws.ts onLog emits only log) shows NO code path ever sends type:'job_start'. So when a new job is spawned via /api/run, /api/replay, /api/selftest, or /api/model-check/scan, the jobs list does NOT refresh immediately — it only updates on the next 5s refreshInterval tick (or the eventual complete/failed). The History view shows stale data for up to 5s after starting a job. This is also a TEMPLATE for usage-aware review: the finding was produced by grep-ing every broadcast site before flagging (the W3 USAGE_AWARE pattern), which is exactly the kind of high-signal finding the post-W4 pipeline should surface. Fix: emit a job_status/job_start broadcast in lib/subprocess.ts spawn() after this.jobs.set(id,job) (broadcastStatus currently fires only on exit), OR frontend-only: also revalidate on a 'log' message when a brand-new jobId appears. FIX ADOPTED 2026-06-20 (feat/gui, server-side option A): lib/subprocess.ts spawn() now calls this.broadcastStatus(job) right after job.pid is assigned (so status='running' fires onStatus early), and api/ws.ts onStatus maps job.status==='running' -> type:'job_start'. Frontend useJobs.ts:16 left unchanged — its job_start listener is now live, so the History list revalidates instantly on spawn instead of lagging up to 5s. bun test 546 pass. Awaiting commit/merge to main; until merged this record's premise (server never broadcasts job_start) still holds on main.

These break on any other machine or worktree. The CORRECT pattern (already used in sibling lib/paths.ts for OUTPUT_DIRS and lib/config.ts for REPO_DIR) is: import { REPO_DIR } from './config'; then path.resolve(REPO_DIR, '..', 'video_generation', 'knowledge-base') with an env override (KB_ROOT / KB_CODE_ROOT) checked first. title: scan.targetScope='full' is reported even on a 2-file incremental effort:low run — do NOT trust targetScope to indicate scan breadth; read totalFiles
detail: 2026-06-20T06:07 (lanes:[review], effort:low, git.headBefore='') reported scan.targetScope='full' YET totalFiles=2, totalLines=412, layers={lib:2} only — i.e. it scanned the 2 working-tree-dirty lib files (code-knowledge.ts + knowledge-db.ts, the files the prior effort:medium+fix:true run modified but had not yet committed). So targetScope='full' is a MISLEADING label: on an effort:low run with a non-empty changed-file set it means 'the resolved scope is the full changed-file set', NOT 'every file in the repo'. The DURABLE discriminator between a true full-surface scan and an incremental one is totalFiles: ~2-10 = incremental (delta on churn); ~190+ = full-surface (effort:medium). Cross-reference with effort:medium-runs-full-scope (which sets totalFiles:191). When a record says targetScope='full', ALWAYS verify totalFiles before treating it as a full-surface count for cross-run comparison — otherwise an incremental 0/1-finding run can be misread as a clean full-surface baseline.
